The expression “Geronimo” is often used when jumping from high heights. It originated in the United States Army during the 1940s. During this time, the U.S. was practicing strategies of dropping troops out of planes for the first time. Before the day of their first jump, a group of paratroopers went out to see a movie. The name of that movie was Geronimo, starring Andy Devine and Chief Thundercloud.



The next day, the troops were scheduled to jump out of a plane for the very first time. One of the troops wanted to prove that he wasn’t scared; so as he was jumping out of the plane, he yelled the name of the movie they all just saw the previous night..

GERONIMOO!

As a result, the other troops yelled the same thing as they jumped out of the plane. The trend caught on like wildfire, and become a global expression.
